summary:
Puebla's recognition regime rests on a 2021 reform of the state civil code adopted by the Puebla congress, which recognised the right to legal gender recognition and was accompanied by a corresponding implementing decree. Human Rights Watch's state-by-state review of 11 March 2025 records that the Puebla regime carries a minimum age of 18 years for recognition, a threshold that has been voided by a court.

On lethal violence, Quadratin reported on 16 June 2026 that of 60 LGBT+ people murdered in Mexico during 2025, 35 were trans women, accounting for 58.3% of the total, with victims in at least 17 states. Puebla recorded the highest raw count of any state, with 7 killings. The ranking is by raw count only; the source provides no per-capita or population denominator, so it does not establish that Puebla is more dangerous for trans people than less populous states.

The same reporting notes documented educational and labour inequality against trans women in Puebla as a standing condition, an everyday-exposure factor alongside the violence figures.
tangentialFactors:
Puebla's raw count of 7 trans and LGBT+ killings in 2025 places it at the top of a state-by-state tally that spans at least 17 states, but the tally is compiled from raw counts with no population adjustment. A state with a large population will tend to accumulate more incidents than a small one regardless of per-capita risk, and the source does not supply the denominator needed to compare states on equal footing.

The court-voiding of the 18-year minimum in Puebla's recognition regime indicates active litigation over the scope of the 2021 reform, and leaves the operative age threshold for recognition unresolved in the sources reviewed here.
localsOnly:
Residents of Puebla seeking legal gender recognition do so under the 2021 state civil code reform and its implementing decree, with the 18-year minimum having been struck down by a court. The current operative age floor is not stated in the sources reviewed.

Trans women in Puebla face documented educational and labour inequality as a standing condition, in addition to the lethal violence recorded for 2025.
outOfScopeNotes:
The current operative minimum age for legal gender recognition in Puebla after the court voided the 18-year threshold is unresolved in the sources reviewed; no source states what age floor, if any, now applies.

Whether Puebla operates an administrative recognition procedure, and how requests are processed in practice, is not sourced here beyond the existence of the 2021 reform and its decree.

The 7 killings attributed to Puebla for 2025 are reported as a raw count with no population denominator; no per-capita figure is available to support comparison with other states.
